title: Knowledge check: jQuery Deferreds and Native Promises

questions.prompt: Which principle best guides a correct implementation of jquery deferreds and native promises?
options: Render user-controlled strings as HTML so the browser can infer their meaning.
Load multiple library copies and rely on whichever one executes last.
Skip error handling and assume the default browser state is always correct.
jqXHR and Deferred APIs support callback-based orchestration. New code should understand native Promises and fetch(), using Deferreds when maintaining an existing jQuery integration.
questions.answer_key: jqXHR and Deferred APIs support callback-based orchestration. New code should understand native Promises and fetch(), using Deferreds when maintaining an existing jQuery integration.
questions.explanation: jqXHR and Deferred APIs support callback-based orchestration. New code should understand native Promises and fetch(), using Deferreds when maintaining an existing jQuery integration. Apply this principle with the API/version documentation linked in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which check is most useful after trying similarities and differences?
options: Use similarities and differences deliberately, then inspect the actual DOM, request, or event result.
Assume the first attempt succeeded and skip verification.
Use a removed jQuery API as the default for new code.
Bind another global handler after every render without cleanup.
questions.answer_key: Use similarities and differences deliberately, then inspect the actual DOM, request, or event result.
questions.explanation: A focused observation checks behavior rather than assuming the method call guarantees the intended result. Include an edge case when the state or inputs can vary.

questions.prompt: Which verification approach best supports professional work with jquery deferreds and native promises?
options: Replace all native browser APIs with jQuery whether needed or not.
Test only the first render and publish immediately.
Move answer keys and private configuration into frontend code.
Test a normal path and a relevant edge/failure path, and record expected versus actual behavior.
questions.answer_key: Test a normal path and a relevant edge/failure path, and record expected versus actual behavior.
questions.explanation: Expected-versus-actual checks, relevant edge cases, and recorded limitations make the implementation easier to debug and review.
